Which report has the highest priority today?
Your team must choose a report to handle first today. Ask which report has the highest priority.
Welke melding is the singular question subject of heeft. Hoogste is the superlative of hoog, describing priority rather than completed work.
The disruption at reception takes priority.
A disruption at reception is more urgent than the other work. State that it takes priority.
Voorrang krijgen means take priority. De storing is singular with krijgt; bij de receptie identifies its location.
We must look at the consequences for customers first.
Your team must assess customer consequences before other considerations. State that first requirement.
Moeten requires bare infinitive bekijken. Eerst puts considering de gevolgen voor klanten before the next action.
What is more urgent: the check or the request?
You need to choose between a check and a request. Ask which is more urgent.
Wat is the question subject. Dringender compares urgency; the two activities after the colon spell out the alternatives.
I give access problems priority over the cleanup work.
You prioritise access problems over cleanup work. Explain that order of priority.
Geef has subject ik. De toegangsproblemen receive voorrang; boven het opruimwerk identifies the work ranked lower.
Not every new report is immediately urgent.
A colleague treats every new report as immediately urgent. Explain why newness does not always mean urgency.
Niet elke means not every, rather than none. Singular melding takes is; dringend is an adjective without -e after is.
Because several teams are stuck, we tackle this problem first.
Several teams are blocked, so your team tackles this problem first. Explain that priority decision.
The omdat-clause gives the reason and ends in vastzitten. Main-clause aanpakken splits as pakken ... aan after the fronted reason.
Can you confirm the order of these tasks?
The task sequence needs confirming before work proceeds. Ask a colleague to confirm the order of these tasks.
Kun precedes je. De volgorde is the order to confirm; confirming it is different from completing the tasks.
The maintenance task can wait until tomorrow.
Maintenance can wait until tomorrow because other work is more urgent. State that deferral option.
Kan expresses possibility, with bare infinitive wachten. Tot morgen sets how long maintenance can wait.
I would like to know what really needs to be finished today.
You need to know which work must actually finish today. Politely ask for that clarification.
Wil graag expresses a wish. The embedded what-question ends in af moet; af describes the required finished state.
I estimate the check will take about an hour.
You estimate that a check will take around an hour. Give that approximate duration.
Schatten op introduces the estimated amount. Ongeveer makes een uur approximate; this is not a guaranteed finishing time.
How much time do you need for preparation?
Preparation needs time that has not been specified. Ask a colleague how much time they need for it.
Hoeveel tijd is the question object. Heb ... nodig means need; voor de voorbereiding gives purpose, not a deadline.
The installation normally takes about twenty minutes.
An installation usually takes roughly twenty minutes. Give that typical duration without guaranteeing it.
Duurt agrees with de installatie. Normaal and ongeveer qualify the typical estimate; twintig minuten is a duration.
S=Ik|MOD=kan|O=de duur|A=beter|I=inschatten|G=als de gegevens compleet zijn.
I can estimate the duration better when the data is complete.
Complete data would let you assess a task's duration better. Explain that condition for improving the estimate.
Kan takes infinitive inschatten. Als introduces the condition and plural de gegevens takes final zijn.
This is an estimate, not a fixed finish time.
A colleague treats your estimate as a fixed finish time. Clarify its provisional status.
Een schatting and geen vaste eindtijd are noun complements after is. Geen rejects a fixed time, not the existence of an estimate.
The previous check took almost two hours.
The previous check took almost two hours. Report that duration as context for estimating.
Heeft geduurd is perfect with singular de vorige controle. Bijna twee uur means almost two hours, not two hours exactly.
Bijna twee uur heeft de vorige controle geduurd.
The previous check took almost two hours.

The same actor, action, time and certainty are retained. This wording changes the first constituent or the position of the time phrase. In a Dutch main clause the finite verb stays second in constituents, with the subject after it when another constituent is fronted.
We must also allow time for feedback.
Your team must include feedback time in the estimate too. State that additional allowance.
Moeten takes rekenen without te. Tijd rekenen means allow time in an estimate; ook adds feedback to the time budget.
This task is bigger than I first thought.
You now realise a task is larger than you initially thought. Revise that earlier assessment.
Groter is comparative, followed by a dan-clause. Dacht is singular past of denken inside that comparison.
Can you update the estimate after the first test?
The first test will provide better evidence for an estimate. Ask a colleague to update the estimate after it.
Kun ... bijwerken is a request. Na de eerste test sets the update after that test, not before it.
There is still a lot of uncertainty in this plan.
The plan still contains much uncertainty. Make that uncertainty explicit to the team.
Er introduces the state. Veel onzekerheid is the singular subject of zit; in deze planning locates the uncertainty figuratively.
Can you look at this with me for ten minutes?
You need a colleague to review something alongside you for ten minutes. Ask for that limited assistance.
Meekijken remains joined after kun. Tien minuten limits the requested time; met mij makes this a joint review rather than complete takeover.
S=Ik|V=heb|O=hulp|C=nodig|PP=bij de controle van de rechten.
I need help checking the permissions.
You need help specifically with checking permissions. Identify that part of the work needing assistance.
Heb ... nodig means need. Hulp is what you need, and bij de controle van de rechten specifies the activity.
I can do the preparation myself.
You can handle preparation without help. State the part of the task you can do independently.
De voorbereiding is a fronted object. Kan comes before subject ik; zelf emphasises independent work and doen stays infinitive.
Will you take over the second check?
You want a colleague to own the second check. Ask them directly to take it over.
Wil jij is a request for willingness. Overnemen stays joined as infinitive; de tweede controle is the limited work being transferred.
S=Ik|V=vraag|O=advies|G=omdat ik deze toepassing nog niet ken.
I ask for advice because I do not know this application yet.
You are unfamiliar with an application, so you are asking for advice. Explain that reason.
Omdat introduces the reason. Ik is its subject and ken is final; nog niet concerns familiarity, not an inability to learn.
We divide the checks between two colleagues.
Your team divides the checks between two colleagues. Describe that allocation of work.
Verdelen over names the people among whom work is distributed. Twee collega's specifies two recipients of the checks.
Can someone briefly read through my findings?
Your findings need a brief read-through by someone else. Ask whether someone can review them.
Kan precedes singular subject iemand. Kort asks for brevity; nalezen is a joined infinitive meaning read through or check.
I do not need someone to take over completely.
You need some help but do not need complete takeover. Explain that limit on assistance.
Geen volledige overname negates a complete transfer. Heb ... nodig expresses need; this does not reject every smaller form of help.
Who has experience with this type of disruption?
You need someone experienced with this type of disruption. Ask who has that relevant experience.
Wie is the question subject. Ervaring met names the relevant experience; dit belongs with singular het type.
G=Als jij de gebruiker belt,|V=werk|S=ik|O=het ticket|PART=bij.
If you call the user, I will update the ticket.
A colleague could call the user while you update the ticket. State that proposed division of work conditionally.
Als jij de gebruiker belt is the condition. Main-clause bijwerken splits as werk ... bij; ik is the person updating the ticket.
I will probably not meet the agreed deadline.
You will probably miss the agreed deadline. Warn the team while keeping the uncertainty explicit.
Waarschijnlijk niet means probably not, rather than certainly not. Haal is present with a future reading for meeting the deadline.
Waarschijnlijk haal ik de afgesproken deadline niet.
I will probably not meet the agreed deadline.

The same actor, action, time and certainty are retained. This wording changes the first constituent or the position of the time phrase. In a Dutch main clause the finite verb stays second in constituents, with the subject after it when another constituent is fronted.
S=De controle|V=duurt|A=langer|G=omdat de gegevens onvolledig zijn.
The check is taking longer because the data is incomplete.
Incomplete data is making a check take longer. Explain why the check is delayed.
Omdat gives the cause. De gegevens is plural with final zijn; langer compares the current duration with the expected one.
We need to move the feedback session to tomorrow.
Your team needs to move the feedback session to tomorrow. Explain the necessary rescheduling.
Moeten takes bare infinitive verplaatsen. Naar morgen sets the new time; the sentence states a need rather than completed rescheduling.
I report the delay now so we can still adjust.
You are reporting a delay now so the team can still adjust. Explain why you are reporting early.
Zodat introduces the intended result, with final kunnen bijsturen. Meld is present; nog says adjustment remains possible.
The delivery has been delayed by two days.
A delivery has incurred two days of delay. Report that amount of delay.
Heeft opgelopen is perfect. Twee dagen vertraging is the amount incurred; it does not name a new scheduled date.
What does this postponement mean for the next task?
A postponement could affect the next task. Ask about its downstream effect.
Wat is the question object, while dit uitstel is the subject of betekent. Voor de volgende taak names the affected work.
The new finish time is not yet certain.
The revised finish time remains unconfirmed. Tell colleagues it is not yet certain.
Nog niet zeker describes uncertainty so far. Zeker is an adjective after is, not a participle reporting a completed action.
Can we move the deadline by one day?
You need an extension of one day to the deadline. Ask whether the team can move it by that amount.
Met één dag specifies the amount of change. Verschuiven alone does not fix its direction; this scenario intends one day later.
G=Zodra ik meer weet,|V=stuur|S=ik|O=een nieuwe schatting.
As soon as I know more, I will send a new estimate.
You will send a new estimate as soon as you know more. State that commitment and trigger.
Zodra introduces the trigger and ends in weet. Main-clause stuur ik follows it; the present can express this future commitment.
Een nieuwe schatting stuur ik zodra ik meer weet.
As soon as I know more, I will send a new estimate.

The same actor, action, time and certainty are retained. This wording changes the first constituent or the position of the time phrase. In a Dutch main clause the finite verb stays second in constituents, with the subject after it when another constituent is fronted.
S=Een deel van het werk|V=is|C=wel klaar.
Part of the work is finished.
Some work is finished even though the whole task is delayed. Point out that partial completion.
Een deel is the singular subject of is. Wel marks positive contrast; klaar does not imply that all work is finished.
Your schedule has no spare capacity today. Explain that it is full.
Mijn planning is singular with zit. Zit vol describes a full schedule figuratively, and vandaag limits that state to today.
I cannot finish both tasks today.
You cannot finish both assigned tasks today. State that capacity limit without claiming neither can finish.
Niet beide means not both, leaving completion of one possible. Kan takes bare infinitive afronden; vandaag limits the claim.
You need permission to defer one task. Ask your team leader which task you may postpone.
Welke taak is the question object, ik the subject of mag. Mogen concerns permission; uitstellen remains infinitive.
S=We|V=hebben|O=te weinig tijd voor alle controles.
We have too little time for all the checks.
There is not enough time for every check. Explain your team's time shortfall.
Te weinig means too little, not merely a small amount. Voor alle controles identifies what the available time cannot cover fully.
Can we divide the work differently?
The current work allocation is impractical. Ask whether your team can divide the work differently.
Kunnen we introduces a joint proposal. Anders means differently and verdelen stays infinitive; no redistribution is reported as completed.
I prefer to take on one task at a time.
You prefer to take responsibility for one task at a time. Express that preference.
Op mij nemen means take upon myself. Liever marks preference; één taak tegelijk limits concurrent responsibility.
S=Ik|V=wil|I=voorkomen|G=dat de kwaliteit onder de tijdsdruk lijdt.
I want to prevent quality from suffering under time pressure.
You want to prevent time pressure harming quality. Explain that concern to your team leader.
Wil takes inseparable voorkomen meaning prevent. The dat-clause ends in lijdt, with de kwaliteit as singular subject.
F=Er|V=is|T=deze week|S=geen ruimte voor extra aanvragen.
There is no capacity for extra requests this week.
Your team has no capacity for extra requests this week. State that weekly limit.
Er introduces the state and geen ruimte is the singular subject of is. Ruimte means capacity here, not a physical room.
For this task, we need a second colleague.
The task needs another colleague in addition to the first. State that extra staffing requirement.
Voor deze taak is fronted, followed by hebben we. Een tweede collega is the additional person needed; nodig completes hebben.
We hebben voor deze taak een tweede collega nodig.
For this task, we need a second colleague.

The same actor, action, time and certainty are retained. This wording changes the first constituent or the position of the time phrase. In a Dutch main clause the finite verb stays second in constituents, with the subject after it when another constituent is fronted.
G=Als dit voorrang krijgt,|V=schuift|S=de andere taak|PART=op.
If this takes priority, the other task moves back.
Prioritising one item will push the other task later. State that conditional trade-off.
Als introduces the priority condition. Opschuiven splits as schuift ... op with singular de andere taak; the consequence is a later slot here.
G=Pas als de toegang werkt,|V=beginnen|S=we|PP=met de controle.
Only when access works do we start the check.
Your team starts the check only once access works. State that access prerequisite.
Pas als means only when. The fronted clause ends in werkt and is followed by beginnen we; met de controle names the activity begun.
S=De test|V=hangt|PP=van de levering van het toestel|PART=af.
The test depends on delivery of the device.
A test cannot proceed until a device is delivered. Explain the delivery dependency.
Afhangen van splits as hangt ... af around the van-phrase. De levering van het toestel is the event on which the test depends.
We need to agree a suitable time first.
Your team must agree a suitable time before the next action. State that scheduling prerequisite.
Moeten takes infinitive afspreken. Eerst sets the order; een geschikt tijdstip has no adjective -e with indefinite singular het tijdstip.
Which task can run alongside the preparation?
Some work might run in parallel with preparation. Ask which task can do so.
Welke taak is the question subject. Kan takes bare infinitive lopen; tegelijk met de voorbereiding names parallel timing.
After approval, we will schedule the change.
Your team will schedule the change after approval. State that order without claiming scheduling is complete.
Na de goedkeuring is fronted, followed by zullen we. Inplannen stays infinitive; approval precedes scheduling in this plan.
We zullen na de goedkeuring de wijziging inplannen.
After approval, we will schedule the change.

The same actor, action, time and certainty are retained. This wording changes the first constituent or the position of the time phrase. In a Dutch main clause the finite verb stays second in constituents, with the subject after it when another constituent is fronted.
S=Een geplande levering|V=is|C=nog geen ontvangen levering.
A scheduled delivery is not a received delivery yet.
A colleague treats a scheduled delivery as already received. Explain why planning is not receipt.
Een geplande levering is the singular subject. Nog geen ontvangen levering is a noun complement; scheduling does not prove receipt.
S=Ik|V=controleer|G=of de leverancier de datum heeft bevestigd.
I check whether the supplier has confirmed the date.
You are checking whether the supplier confirmed the date. Describe that verification without asserting confirmation.
Of introduces a whether-question. De leverancier is its singular subject, with final perfect group heeft bevestigd.
The next step can only start after the check.
The next step cannot start until the check is over. Explain that sequence constraint.
Kan takes infinitive beginnen. Pas na de controle means only after the check, rather than allowing it before that point.
We keep room for an extra test round.
Your team keeps capacity for an extra test round. Describe that allowance in the plan.
Ruimte houden voor means keep capacity for. Een extra testronde is a potential additional round, not a claim that it has already occurred.
G=Voordat ik verlof neem,|V=draag|S=ik|O=de openstaande taken|PART=over.
Before I take leave, I hand over the outstanding tasks.
You will hand over outstanding tasks before taking leave. State that handover plan.
Voordat introduces the earlier handover boundary. The fronted clause is followed by draag ik; overdragen splits as draag ... over.
